newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico Cetes rate ends off but pressure persists.
newsitem.headline: Mexico Cetes rate ends off but pressure persists.

text.p: Mexico's overnight Cetes rate closed down 130 basis points at 29.20 percent on Monday, but traders said rates were still under pressure
Traders said Monday's close was only low in comparison to an unrepresentative high close on Friday.
"Government rates were inflated. Pressure from some dealers had narrowed down the spread between government and bank paper to marginal levels," a trader said.
Pressure was still evident, traders noted, as overnight rates had reached a session high of 30.30 percent.
Overnight rates on bank paper also closed down, by 35 basis points, at 30.95 percent.
Traders said rates were under pressure from Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee meeting to review U.S. interest rates, and from year-end demand for liquidity.
"The FOMC meeting allowed pressure exerted by some to take effect," a dealer said.
Dealers said the central bank's daily liquidity injection eased the pressure on secondary rates.
Banco de Mexico offset liquidity shortfalls by injecting 3.982 billion pesos through three credit auctions, which it injected at between 30.88 percent and 30.98 percent.
Nonetheless some dealers foresaw government overnight rates opening up again on Tuesday, to narrow the gap with bank rates.
"In theory, with bank rates being where they are, government paper should be trading at 29.60 percent," one trader said.
Credit maturities for Tuesday were expected to total 6.277 billion pesos.
